title: Stampede
logline: Dawn in a sleeping city. A six storey {product} drops into the plaza fountain, and two giant red bulls charge off it down the avenue, switching the whole city on as they run.

world.rules: Every storefront sign, billboard, bus stop and screen is blank. The only readable brand anywhere is the product, and only on the can itself. The billboard in the final shot is a blank white panel for post text.

beats.summary: A sleeping city at dawn. Something enormous falls out of the sky and lands in the plaza fountain with a boom.
One early runner stops dead, earbud out, and looks up at it.
The reveal orbit: a six storey can dripping car-sized drops, label square to camera. Then two giant red bulls step out of a burst of gold light at its base.
The bulls charge down the avenue. Every streetlight, window and tram lights up in their wake; the runner sprints beside them, laughing.
At the waterfront the bulls leap into the rising sun and the whole skyline is switched on.
The giant can stands in the now busy plaza; the runner holds a normal can at its base. Brand line, tagline, blank billboard filled in post.

music.brief: Near silence, one high sustained string note rising with the falling can, cut to nothing on the impact so the boom lands in silence, then a single low piano note.
Slow brass swell in C minor under the orbit, taiko hits on each hoof as the bulls step out.
Driving 128 bpm trailer percussion with galloping 6/8 toms, brass ostinato, lifting a step at the drone shot, peak at the leap into the sun.
Resolves to C major, bright brass chord and a light shaker, ring out past the last frame under the VO.

lore: Calloway is a fictional harbour city of 1.4 million on a cold northern bay. Founders' Plaza sits at the top of Ferris Avenue, a dead-straight 2 km run down to the ferry piers.
The Founders' Fountain was carved in 1911 from grey granite: a round basin 30 metres across with four bronze dolphin spouts, green with verdigris, restored last spring.
It is 6:04am on a Tuesday in late October. The first Harbor Line tram of the day leaves the plaza at 6:10; the street sweeper has just passed and the paving is still wet.
Jae Park runs the same 8 km loop at this hour every weekday, plaza to piers and back, and has never once seen the city switch on before him.
Kettle & Oar, the corner cafe on the plaza, opens at 6:30; its chairs are still stacked and chained under the striped awning.
